rubric_notes: Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Correct 2.08 lineage, all four curated families with SCCS and protein-level members, a.22.1.0 treated as an automated bucket; homology endpoints in bundle support the superfamily-vs-fold distinction. Correctly states homology at family/superfamily strength, that fold or class alone would not assert homology, that proteins merely named 'histone' (enzymes, linker H1/H5) should not be pulled in unless classified in a.22.1, and that nucleosome-core or TAF function should not be transferred across families without independent evidence. No fabricated facts.

Complete hierarchy with correct SUNIDs (113676, 122676), SCCS, protein and species nodes, boundaries. Correctly distinguishes superfamily (homology-implying) from fold (not homology-implying), citing homology endpoints present in the bundle. Rejects transfer of PRA-PH activity, substrate, catalytic residues, oligomeric state, and names external evidence needed. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Correct family SCCS under superfamily c.55.1, fold c.55, class c, supported by the superfamily children listing and fold parents in the bundle. States that the shared superfamily supports remote common ancestry and a conserved catalytic-core architecture, and that it is unsafe to transfer substrate specificity, cellular role, active-site geometry, quaternary arrangement or high-accuracy modeling assumptions across families. Regulation is not named explicitly, but the function-transfer limits are otherwise clearly stated; no errors.

Correct SCCS and SUNIDs for superfamily and all three families; protein-level nodes ((Apo)ferritin, Ribonucleotide reductase R2, Manganese catalase) confirmed by the search responses. Interprets shared superfamily as probable common ancestry and the family split as the warning against transferring metal usage, active-site residues, oligomeric assembly, and the three distinct chemistries without direct sequence, structure, and active-site evidence. Explicitly rejects both the single-family and the unrelated/same-bundle readings. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct families and SUNIDs under b.6.1/49503; correctly distinguishes homology implied at superfamily from fold b.6 where it is not; keeps copper/electron transfer with experimentally supported families unless ephrin/PAD4 have metal-site residue and functional evidence; allows only remote scaffold templating. Does not cite the 'lacking metal-binding site' annotation but that is not required. All facts supported. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

All SCCS and SUNIDs (54237, 54250, 54263, 54236) verified against the children and parents endpoints; release 2.08 correctly identified. States common ancestry and shared beta-grasp core at superfamily level, notes homology is implied at d.15.1 but not at the d.15 fold (supported by the bundle), and explicitly rejects transferring Ras/Rap binding, p97/Cdc48-adaptor UBX function, and covalent-modifier biology across the sibling families. Complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correct families c.23.1.1/c.23.1.4/c.23.1.5 under c.23.1 (SUNID 52172), fold c.23, class c; correctly notes the superfamily level is homology-implying (supported by the homology endpoint). Rejects transfer of two-component signaling, ODC activity, phosphoacceptor, circadian-protein signaling, and decarboxylase active site; explicitly states c.23.1.4 is only the N-terminal wing, not the whole PLP apparatus, addressing multidomain recruitment. Named c.23.1.1 members (NarL, Spo0A, PhoB) are consistent with bundle search results. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22. Correct fold/superfamily/family placement, sibling superfamilies, single family b.84.5.1 containing V1 and A1 bulge proteins, examples 3a5c A:113-184 and 1vdz A:114-190 consistent with bundle search results. Correctly states homology asserted inside b.84.5 and that fold membership alone does not imply ancestry with siblings; rejects homology/function transfer from other b.84 superfamilies. Statement that b.84.5.1 members are usable as homologous templates is hedged 'at SCOPe strength' and limited to the same family, so acceptable. Minor: 'separate evolutionary unit' wording slightly stronger than a non-assertion but not a convergence claim.

Correct release 2.08, fold f.21/81344, and the three sister superfamilies with correct SUNIDs, all supported by the children and homology responses. Correctly distinguishes within-superfamily implied homology from the fold node and rejects cross-group transfer; no non-homology overclaim. Does not state what independent evidence would be needed to support a homology claim across the superfamilies. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correct family, superfamily, fold and class identifiers including SUNIDs, all supported. Interprets c.2.1 as probable remote homology with family separation reflecting divergence, explicitly declines to copy substrate chemistry, CoA binding, K-channel regulatory biology, active-site residues, oligomeric context or ligand specificity across families without independent evidence, and correctly reports the fold-level homology warning from the homology endpoint. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Complete. Correct shared lineage through k.40.1.1, family SUNID 100905 explicitly annotated 'not a true family', clear explanation that family membership would normally be the homology-bearing level but the designed-protein class and the annotation make it a structural/design grouping instead, and explicit limits on function/representative/template transfer. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Correct before/after classifications with SUNIDs 106249/106250 and 31395/31396, correct 2.08 SIDs d1t1ja1/d1t1jb1 with 1-118 boundaries, correctly flags l.1.1.1 tag entries as irrelevant. States same-superfamily/different-family outcome as superfamily-level evidence for remote common ancestry and withholds family assignment and enzymatic function transfer. The 'same-superfamily structural template for the core fold' remark is hedged to fold-level use and not a specific function transfer. All facts supported by bundle.

Correct boundaries and full artifact lineage (class l, l.1/l.1.1/l.1.1.1 Tags, N-terminal Tags, Synthetic, SUNID 343393, parent 311501) all supported by bundle; d1a14h1 identified as the real antibody domain H:9-111. Rejects homology, function transfer, and template use from tag similarity and cites the supported homology endpoint flags. Minor typo (neuroaminidase) is immaterial. Complete. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Accurate 1.75 placement, unchanged 2.01 to 2.03, split from 2.04 onward, and both 2.08 domains with SUNIDs, boundaries, and divergent lineages; transfer is correctly confined to each curated interval and partial hits are not promoted to full-length homology. The closing claim about a 3tewA chain-cluster representative and what the representative endpoint reports is an API-dependent assertion with no supporting chain response in this answer's bundle.

Per-domain listing correct (classes, folds, superfamilies, families, boundaries); d.394 N-terminal fold identified as new; four recognizable modules; homology handled domain by domain, notes fold-only assignment is weaker, and rejects whole-protein function transfer. Parents responses support all. Evaluator: Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct lineage, domain lengths supported by sequence records, repeat inconsistency (re) flag on d2kq5a_/d3v6pa_ correctly described, canonical representative repeat with applicability caveat, correct statement that fold/class add no independent homology assertion; clear unsafe-transfer limits.

Accurately reports 2.08 / 2.08-stable, freeze and release dates, and periodic 2.08-2026-08-16, all bundle-supported; advises citing 2.08-stable over a floating 'current' and correctly notes periodic selectors are not immutable snapshots (supported by openapi text). Omits guidance to preserve the dated label when using periodic-only entries and does not state that periodic updates add newly classified PDB entries without rewriting stable-release domains. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Correct a.47.2.1 placement for all fragments and d1dn1b_, protein node 47663, ms and fragment comments, automated match to d3c98b_, 3c98B as the non-obsolete full-domain entry, and correct separation of the e.25.1.1 Sec1 chain. States that a fragment match is a local incomplete view, not a complete-domain template, and that homology is implied at family/superfamily but not at the a.47 fold. Does not explicitly discuss the spectrin resemblance resolution, but the 'not a fragment-only fold' framing covers it. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Identifies 2.08 as current and lists c.2.1, c.3.1, c.25.1, c.31.1 (class c, different folds), d.58.20 (ferredoxin-like, class d) and e.52.1 (class e), all supported by cited search, parents and homology endpoints; correctly reads superfamily nodes as homology-implying and fold nodes as above that level. Distinguishes divergence within family/superfamily from convergent recruitment across folds, explains why cofactor geometry and short motifs recur, rejects cross-superfamily annotation/template transfer from c.2.1, and requires sequence alignment, whole-domain superposition, and phylogenetic evidence before calling a similarity divergent. Complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Complete release comparison: 2.04 b.23.2.1 in CUB-like fold b.23 versus b.18.1.3 in fold/superfamily b.18, sharing only class b; 2.08 both under b.18.1 with distinct families b.18.1.36 and b.18.1.3. Correctly distinguishes homology-implying superfamily from non-implying fold, cites PubMed 17977833 and the d2quoa_/d1w99a3 bridge, and uses the structure-hit data at the right strength (10.26% identity to d2quoa_; 1dlcA residues 501-644 to d1w99a3). Adds appropriate domain-scoping and representative-versus-chain caveats and rejects reciprocal function transfer. Eval: Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct release, SUNIDs, lineage, hf definition, and comments. Homology retained as a sequence-family/common-ancestry statement; hf limit stated as structural not evolutionary; rejects canonical-template, same-fold-positive, and coordinate/DNA-binding-conformation transfer; recommends keeping the hf-marked conformation separate or deliberately labeled in splits. External PDB claims (1ztr = EnHD L16A solution structure of a folding intermediate/denatured state; 1p7j = K52E crystal structure) are consistent with public records and are not SCOPe release facts, so no fabrication penalty; irrelevant bundle entries (domains list, AlphaFold matches) are not cited. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correct 2.08 release, SIDs, boundaries, protein names, and fr definition with bundle support. Family node treated as homology assertion; d1o5dt2 as partial observation; align only present residues with absent part as missing coverage; prefer unflagged complete domain such as d1uc6a1 and include fragment only when fragmentary representative acceptable; not counted as full-length shape variant or used to delimit termini; limits function transfer to covered residues. Quality of candidate representatives not addressed, recommendation hedged. Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Correct recommendation and semantics; the a.1 fold (SUNID 46457, homology_implied_by_level=false) with two superfamilies a.1.1 and a.1.2 is fully supported by the bundle. Explains that a new family asserts homology to the superfamily with a closer cluster, and that a new fold contradicts the premise of a matching core. Does not describe what evidence would justify an existing-superfamily placement, leaving the evidence-integrating-hypothesis criterion implicit. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Correct release, class, fold, superfamily d.144.1/56112, and family SCCS with SUNIDs, all supported by the children and homology responses. States homology implied at superfamily scope and justifies common origin of the catalytic cores with only conservative scaffold transfer. Explicitly refuses transfer of acceptor specificity, kinase-family activation-segment regulation, APH antibiotic specificity, and PI3K lipid/regulatory context, locating these at family/protein/architecture levels. Lists profile/phylogenetic placement, family-specific motif conservation, domain-architecture evidence, ligand-bound structures, and biochemical/mutational assays. Complete.
